output.myth: Kael the Netter cast for fallen stars every night off the Leeward Reach, and every night they slipped his mesh like wet fish. He went to Ennu the Kite-Wright and asked for a better needle. Ennu gave him a mending shuttle of bone, pointed at both ends, with thread wound round its belly. "Work with it," Ennu said, "and your hands will never be idle." Kael took it into the dark and mended cords all night. He never caught a star. But at dawn the shuttle was gone from his fingers, and a thread ran from its place straight up into the sky. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, has marked it. Some say the shuttle is still up there, still mending, and that the thread is a line let out for the drowned to climb. Fishers who lose a man at sea tell the Netter his name and wait. He gives no one back. But he listens, which is more than the sea does.
output.verse:
Kael the Netter casts
a thread runs up from his hand
still mending the sky
